title: Digital arrest scams - the new fraud everyone should know about
p1: Your phone rings. A stranger claims you are involved in a serious crime. They sound official, use legal words, and tell you not to disconnect. Many people panic within minutes. But what if the entire "investigation" is fake?
p2: The surprising truth: there is no such thing as a digital arrest. Scammers create fear by pretending to be police officers, government officials, or bank representatives. They use video calls, fake documents, and pressure tactics to make victims believe they are under real investigation.
p3: The biggest warning sign is urgency. Real authorities do not ask you to transfer money to prove your innocence or keep a secret investigation running through a phone call. If someone threatens you and demands immediate action, pause, verify independently, and never share passwords, OTPs, or banking details. A calm response can protect you from a costly mistake.
conclusion: Have you or someone you know received a suspicious call claiming to be from a police or government department? What was your first reaction?
